QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_21

question.text: Compliance with SAS is mandatory under the SEBI framework for social impact assessments conducted for:

answer.text: All Indian NPOs regardless of SSE listing
Only Section 8 Companies with annual turnover above INR 100 crore
Social enterprises listed on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE)
Only CSR programmes of the top 500 listed companies

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.5 'Compliance with SAS' sub-section states: 'Compliance with SAS is a mandatory requirement for social impact assessment conducted for social enterprises listed on social stock exchange.' If the SIA cannot comply, the report must draw attention to material departures. The Trap: A overshoots — SAS compliance is mandatory only for SSE-listed SEs, though SIAs are encouraged to follow SAS for other engagements too. B invents a turnover threshold. D conflates with the CSR rule 8(3) impact-assessment trigger. Cross-Exam Context: NISM III-A / III-C tests SEBI mandatory-compliance boundaries. XXIII's nuance: SAS is mandatory for SSE-listed, voluntary but recommended for other engagements. Assessor's Pro-Tip: On non-SSE engagements (e.g. CSR rule 8(3) assessments), still apply SAS and state in your report: 'This engagement has been conducted applying the principles of SAS framework issued by ICAI SIAB' — it lifts the quality bar and simplifies future SSE migration of the SE.
